Check Object Names Against the Calling Frames and the Search Path

Source: R/env_check.R
env_check.Rd

Checks whether the object names of an environment are also used in the environments above it: the frames of the call stack (sys.frames(): the calling functions, not the environments where the functions are defined), then the search path (search()). Useful to detect object names of a function, or of the global environment, that mask or are masked by other objects.

Usage

env_check(
  pos = 1,
  name = NULL,
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

pos

Single positive integer: position of the checked environment in the call stack, counted from env_check(), then in the search path. 1 (default) checks the environment that calls env_check(): the frame of a function, or the global environment at top level. 2 checks the environment one step further up, etc., up to package:base, the last environment of the search path.

name

Single character string: name of the checked environment in the returned message (e.g., the name of the function calling env_check()). If NULL (default), "UNNAMED" for the frame of a function, or the name of an environment of the search path (e.g., ".GlobalEnv").

safer_check

Single logical value. If TRUE (default), checks before running that the required packages and functions are installed and that the classical R operators (like <-) are not masked by another package or by a user-defined object of the global environment. These checks take time at each call: set FALSE in loops and inside other safer-r functions, to avoid repeating them.

lib_path

Vector of character strings: paths of existing extra library folders containing the required packages (e.g., packages installed without admin rights). They are searched after the current .libPaths() during the call (the current libraries keep priority), and .libPaths() is restored on exit. If NULL (default), only the current .libPaths() are used.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages (e.g., " INSIDE pkg1::fun1()") to name the calling functions. NULL is converted into "".

Value

A character string listing, for each environment above the checked one, the object names it shares with the checked environment, followed by the environments checked (frames written <environment>). NULL if no name is shared.

Details

Call env_check() directly (e.g., res <- env_check()), not inside another call like print(env_check()) or cat(env_check()), which would check the frame of print() or cat() instead. At the top level of code run by source() or knitr, the frames of the functions running the code are also checked.

See also

sys.frames, search.

Author

Gael Millot

Haiding Wang

Yushi Han

Examples

# Warning: the "Run examples" link also checks the frames of the code running the examples.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/env_check.html
# Inside a function: the names t.test and mean, created inside fun1(),
# also exist in the stats and base environments located above:
fun1 <- function(){
    t.test <- 0
    mean <- 5
    saferDev::env_check(pos = 1, name = "fun1", safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL,
        error_text = "")
}
a <- fun1()
base::cat(a, file = "", sep = " ", fill = FALSE, labels = NULL, append = FALSE)
#> SOME VARIABLES OF THE CHECKED ENVIRONMENT fun1 ARE ALSO PRESENT IN :
#> package:stats: t.test
#> package:base: mean
#> SEARCH PATH CHECKED:

# NULL returned when no name is also present in the environments above:
fun2 <- function(){
    tempo_name_used_nowhere_else <- 0
    saferDev::env_check(pos = 1, name = "fun2", safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL,
        error_text = "")
}
fun2()
#> NULL
# The frames of the calling functions are checked (call stack), here the frame of fun3():
fun3 <- function(){
    min <- 1
    fun4()
}
fun4 <- function(){
    min <- 2
    saferDev::env_check(pos = 1, name = "fun4", safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL,
        error_text = "")
}
a <- fun3()
base::cat(a, file = "", sep = " ", fill = FALSE, labels = NULL, append = FALSE)
